title: **Public checker reliability, discovery and free-install
notes: conversion:** Deployed runtime `6daca9d`. SPF follows bounded
include/redirect dependencies, detects cycles and missing policies, and
distinguishes transient failures. DMARC discovers inherited policies
through the RFC 9989 DNS tree walk, identifies their source and accounts
for subdomain/test policies. Known DKIM selectors are validated and
retained in report URLs and copied links.
- Search evidence: The dedicated public Search Console property is verified.
Google fetched the sitemap with zero errors/warnings and one discovered URL.
The live homepage test passed and its priority indexing request was
accepted. Indexing and rankings remain pending; the initial sitemap HTTP
error cleared without weakening Cloudflare security.
- Deployment: The owner-authorized Cache Purge credential is zone-scoped and
stored outside the repository with owner-only permissions. The automated
deployment command preserves the previous runtime and startup configuration,
performs a four-URL purge and runs the public boundary/DNS verifier.
result: The sole conversion is the free self-hosted installation. Optional Analytics starts after acceptance and excludes scanned domains, selectors and DNS records from transport. Enhanced automatic collection is disabled; installation clicks are a key event, not proof of completed installation. Private deployments without explicit public configuration load no Google tag.
evidence: `pnpm exec vitest run --config vitest.config.mts --maxWorkers=4 --testTimeout=30000 --hookTimeout=30000` passed (195 files, 1,031 tests). The default five-second budget hit existing Triage and ingest-fixture timeouts under machine load; application assertions were unchanged. Focused DNS tests passed after the final case-handling update. Types, ESLint, oxlint, knip, dependency boundaries, formatting, migrations and chart checks passed. Linux standalone build and private Analytics isolation passed. The production deployment command and public verifier passed; browser checks passed consent/rejection, selector sharing/reload and mobile overflow. Actual Google collection returned HTTP 204 with sanitized payloads and no Analytics CSP errors. Vexa Mail remained HTTP 200.
